sources.concept: rapid HTTP/2 request creation and reset by remote client

impact.affected_asset: Availability and compute resources of the HTTP/2 server process.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote HTTP/2 client can drive excessive concurrent handler work by repeatedly creating requests and immediately resetting them.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through excessive server resource consumption.

causal_trace.summary: A malicious HTTP/2 client rapidly creates requests and immediately resets them.
Resetting an in-progress request lets the client create a new request while the handler for the reset request is still executing, so the stream limit does not bound simultaneously executing handlers.
The server continues to execute handler goroutines for reset in-flight requests while accepting replacement requests, permitting handler work to grow beyond MaxConcurrentStreams.
The resulting excessive handler work causes excessive server resource consumption.

failure.operation: Execution of handler goroutines beyond the configured HTTP/2 stream concurrency limit after rapid request resets.

primary_invariant.statement: The number of simultaneously executing HTTP/2 handler goroutines must not exceed the stream concurrency limit, MaxConcurrentStreams.
primary_invariant.violated_because: A reset removes an in-progress request from the request/stream concurrency accounting sufficiently to allow a replacement request, although the original request handler continues executing.

quality.review_notes: The reviewed advisory and issue establish the request-reset mechanism, affected scope, and intended mitigation. Gerrit patch artifacts in this bundle have empty text excerpts, and no regression-test source, reproducer, or execution result is available; no test oracle or observed reproduction is asserted.

remediation.invariant_restored: Simultaneously executing handler goroutines are bounded by MaxConcurrentStreams; requests received after resets are queued until a handler exits, with oversized queues causing connection termination.
mitigation_classes: bound concurrent handler execution to stream limit
queue requests that arrive at the handler limit
terminate connection when the request queue becomes too large

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker uses one HTTP/2 connection to rapidly create requests and immediately reset them while their handlers remain in progress.
data_structure_invariants: The advertised stream concurrency setting must also bound active handler goroutines.
After an in-flight reset, replacement requests at the handler limit must wait for a handler exit.
An excessively large queued-request backlog causes connection termination.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The advisory states a default of 250 streams per HTTP/2 connection; the setting is configurable.
numeric_domains.name: MaxConcurrentStreams

state_context.state_machine: An HTTP/2 request begins handler execution; a client can reset the in-flight request and submit a replacement before the original handler exits.
